title: Murr the Old Wolf
type: Voraketh wolf, guide, and surviving witness
dek: An old wolf who knows the island’s paths and remembers an earlier world, while Voraketh erodes the memories she carries.

facts.Near the Chains: Reports losing thought and falling into instinct

sources: Murr_the_Old_Wolf_NPC_Master.md — supplied 5 October 2026; quest-RP parts 029, 033, 034; public testimony separated from master-only clarification
Quest RP refreshed source · supplied 23 October 2026 · 3,845 messages across the main channel and two accessible threads; posting chronology and narrated continuations remain distinct
body:
Murr the Old Wolf is an aged, scarred, speaking wolf native to Voraketh. She knows its woods, scents, paths, and dangers, and remembers fragments of an island different from the one the explorers encounter. Important parts of that history have been taken from her.

Her clouded amber eyes, ash-and-shadow coat, scarred muzzle, and deliberate movement show her age. Strength remains beneath the old body, but by May 2026 she pants more easily and rises with difficulty. Her exact age is unknown.

27 October 2025: the occupied camp

Murr emerges from the woods and warns the strangers: “Easy now. If I meant harm, you’d already know it.” She already knows Coralyn and St. Anky Bloomers III. Anky calls her wondrous and says he has written about her in a scroll left in the magic tree. Their earlier meetings are not recovered.

She evaluates outsiders through scent and intent: are they hunting, hiding, or unaware of what they have entered? Carmen smells of “ash and old storms.” Murr calls adventuring groups packs and tracks people by their distinctive odors, even when she does not know their names.

A guide who expects to be heard

The woods have been her domain for a long time. When she guides a group, she expects it to follow her pace and step where she steps. Near the “singing chains,” her instructions become urgent: draw close, stay low, and move slowly and quietly.

The dangers do not always announce themselves. Some Chains screech, others move quietly, and some threats leave no scent. Murr becomes nervous and frightened on the approach, yet continues because she promised to guide the group.

If you won’t hide, then learn to walk quiet.Murr the Old Wolf

Her authority rests on survival knowledge. She recognizes competence without accepting bravado as protection, and keeps firm boundaries around how far she will risk her own life.

The island she remembers

Murr describes Voraketh as sick. In her account, darkness leaks from its heart, the Chains slow the spread, and order and chaos both rot. She says life and death have forgotten their places. These are her observations and interpretations, not a complete explanation of the island.

She preserves competing traditions about the Chains: perhaps the land was bound too tightly to keep darkness out; perhaps the bindings keep something beyond from coming through. Her own warning is that chains hold rather than heal.

Maybe I once knew the answers to your questions.Murr the Old Wolf

The Chains are older than her available memory. She also reports that reaching them took days when she was a pup, while the journey is now shorter. Whether that reflects changed geography, distance, memory, or another cause remains unresolved.

Old spirits and possible healing

Pappy asks whether the island can heal. Murr softens: perhaps, but not by tooth or claw. She believes the place remembers what it was and imagines hands and hearts remembering with it. Restoration remains a hope rather than a proven method.

She recognizes Pappy’s old spiritual language and says few still speak to the old spirits, fewer listen. She has had no connection to the ancestors for many moons. The nature of that earlier connection and the cause of its loss are unknown.

24 April 2026: the cost of approaching

Murr reports that a pack-mate has died; the party identifies him as Cirilo. She believes he went too close to the Chain. She helps track other missing adventurers by scent and mentions a large shore cave that appeared suddenly, without supplying its origin.

She guides the group toward the body, then refuses to go farther. The Chain and its shining monsters are deadly, and she has no desire to risk her life for a corpse.

Asked why she helps people who might overcome the Chain, she gives a personal answer: perhaps things could be as they once were, and she could run with her pack again. The record leaves the pack’s fate unknown and does not establish that removing a Chain would restore it.

I quickly begin to lose myself, falling into pure instinct. Losing thought.Murr the Old Wolf

That is Murr’s own description of what happens near the Chain. Her boundary protects her thought as well as her body. Asked why she can speak at all, she does not know: perhaps she was always this way.

28 May 2026: the upright folk

Murr remembers former inhabitants, long gone, whom she calls the “upright folk.” She has not seen a book since their time. Their identity and relationship with her remain unknown; the phrase is her description rather than an established faction name.

Details have been taken from her, she says, as a river takes a stone. She compares recovering memory to returning to a lost scent.

Ithilrûnë Ailinor considers whether the Veiled Watch might help. Murr is curious and goes there, but the surviving scene shows no immediate recovery. Old caves and places of former habitation remain possible leads, without a guarantee that they will restore her memories.

The explorers around her

Coralyn’s familiarity and Anky’s questions draw out Murr’s testimony. Pappy shares a language of age, nature, and spirits. Ithilrûnë presses for reasons and later considers how to help her memory. Carmen’s sharpness meets an equally stubborn response. Sildithas encounters her through Coralyn’s accounts and asks about her losses.

Murr remains independent. She offers practical help, warnings, and historical fragments while refusing the role of an all-knowing elder. Her lost memories, pack, ancestors, origin of speech, and later fate remain open.

The remembered name of the refuge

The adventurers at the Last Grove remember Murr naming the sanctuary and speaking of lost natural cycles and older animals that remember more. These are their reports of his earlier conversations, rather than a new encounter at the tree.

The blight reaches an old guide

The October expedition finds Murr sick in the spreading fungal blight. Coralyn’s healing gives only brief relief, while Pappy also tries to help. Ithilrûnë feels infernal corruption distinct from Delerium; Sildithas adds cleansing strength as Ithilrûnë reaches for it. Murr rises and thanks Sildithas.

Questions about a half-remembered name bring fragments of a maternal figure rather than a secure identity. Repeated utterances are followed by waves that shake the group and knock Murr down. Her recovered strength does not establish that all her memory has returned. She later limps toward the Grove while the company divides over what to tackle next.
